3: ## Overview
4: 
5: `vercel routes` manages project-level routing rules. Each rule matches requests by path pattern and optional conditions (headers, cookies, query parameters), then applies an action (rewrite, redirect, set status) or modifies headers and query parameters.
6: 
7: Routing rules take effect immediately without a deployment and take precedence over routes defined in your deployment configuration (`vercel.json`, `next.config.js`, etc.).
8: 
9: Each routing rule has a unique name within the project, used to identify it in `edit`, `delete`, `enable`, `disable`, and `reorder` commands. Rules are evaluated in priority order (top to bottom). Use `reorder` to control placement.
10: 
11: All changes are staged as drafts. Run `vercel routes publish` to push staged changes to production.
12: 
13: ## Viewing Routing Rules
14: 
15: ```bash
16: vercel routes list                       # all routing rules
17: vercel routes list --diff                # staged changes vs production
18: vercel routes inspect "My Route"         # full details of a specific rule
19: ```
